note: The arc rules (src/arc.ts): where a signature part plays over a track's form, as a producer of its genre places it: withheld, teased, exposed in runs, then the peak (his rule, 10-28). A part names a rule by id (the hook row's `arc`). `sections`, by the section's kind: `tease` bars at the track's start; `end` a run at the section's end after `groove` bars of it; `from` a run from that share of the section, on the `step` grid; `continues` the run reaching into it; `into` the kind joins only straight into a run; `short` the kind joins only where the part's share would fall under `share`'s bottom without it. Runs cut in and out; every run of `breakFrom` bars or more ends in `breakBars` of the part alone, unless it runs into a kind of `noBreakInto`; the runs are shaped so none is longer than the last (the peak): a run a main's end opens is shortened from its front (a longer groove first), any other from its end (a hard cut, the section's groove going on, no break of the part alone); and shortened from the first while the share of the track is over `share`'s top. `knobs`: any quantity ramped from the first run to the peak (the runs between in step), with its value in the tease; the part reads them in its own units.

units.says: bars are the theme's written grid; `from` a share of the section; `share` a share of the track; a knob is the part's own unit (the hook's two are dB)

rows.says: the trance hook: a shallow tease in the intro, runs at the mains' ends after a groove, the drop's whole, a build only into a drop and only where the share would fall short, an outro the run reaches; the chop's depth and the level ramped to the peak
